name: Hemam
overview: Hemam was a male Edomite, known primarily as the son of Lotan. He is identified in Scripture as part of the Edomite lineage, reflecting his heritage within the descendants of Esau. Beyond this, the biblical record provides no additional details about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Hemam appears in Genesis 36:22, with an alternate form, Homam, found in 1 Chronicles 1:39. Neither name is given a specific meaning or divine origin in the biblical text, so they are understood simply as proper names without further significance provided.
familyAndRelationships: Hemam is explicitly recorded as the son of Lotan, establishing his direct family connection within the Edomite genealogy. Scripture does not provide any other family relationships for Hemam beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Hemam's significance lies in his place within the Edomite genealogical records, which trace the descendants of Esau. By being named as a son of Lotan, Hemam contributes to the biblical understanding of the Edomite tribes and their origins. His mention preserves the historical lineage important for comprehending the broader narrative of God's dealings with the descendants of Abraham's brother.
